cells.tense: You are here at the beginning of a clear seeing, before there's anything specific to see.
cells.ask: Name one thing you noticed today that you haven't said out loud, and say it to someone.
cells.core:
You're at the front edge of noticing. Not looking for anything in particular — just the switch flipped on, the first cut before it has anything to cut. That's a beginning, and beginnings don't need content yet. They need you to stay with them a little longer than is comfortable.

What's free to feed here is depth. You want to go further into what you're noticing, to see how it connects. That works when it comes from real understanding, and the test is simple: do the patterns you find let something move? Say one thing you've seen this week to someone who can hear it. Noticing gets real in the saying.
cells.sheetLine: You're here for the start of clear noticing. Stay and let it speak.
cells.verb: seeing clearly before the object of seeing arrives

cells.tense: A clear seeing is coming and you are already bracing for what it might mean.
cells.ask: Put the planning aside for one hour and be somewhere new without deciding what it means yet.
cells.core:
This looks like a mind that won't sit still. Something's arriving and before it lands, you've mapped what it will demand, where it leads, what you'll have to do about it. The bracing runs ahead of the moment. It runs ahead of you.

The other face of this is being open and available, letting each moment be new. Not shining to prove you already see — just present enough to receive what's here. The depth isn't the problem. The pressure on top of it is. Let one thing be fresh without deciding what it means. That's not losing the sight. That's letting it actually come in.
cells.sheetLine: You're bracing for something before it's arrived. Let it come.

cells.tense: A clear seeing arrived a while back and you are still standing at the door behind it.
cells.ask: Take one small step today on something you already see clearly, without waiting to feel ready.
cells.core:
You noticed something — a pattern, a direction, a truth about how things are — and instead of turning with it, you stayed where you were. The door was there. You never crossed it. What's absent isn't more insight. It's moving from what's already in front of you.

The far side of this is direction and the present lining up: you act from what you see, not from compulsion or habit. Pick one small thing that calls for and do it today. Not because you feel ready. Because what you see is enough to stand on, and the step itself is what carries you through.

cells.tense: You are already the turning where what's outside becomes what enters here.
cells.ask: Say out loud what you're already noticing, as if you're the one who noticed it.
cells.core:
You're doing it right now. Something's coming in and you're the place it comes through — not watching from a distance, being where it lands. But you describe it as if it arrived on its own, or as if anyone standing here would see the same thing.

The doing is happening. The owning isn't. You point at what you notice instead of saying that you're the one noticing. That's not modesty. It's a misstatement of what's actually going on. When you recognize yourself as the turning — not the witness of it, the place it happens — what you see becomes yours to work with. Say one thing you're already noticing, as yours. That's not ego. That's accuracy.

attempts.check: The record supports the mechanism—Perception as Actualization through Cognition, appearing in Source, with the four statuses. It does not support any claim about what the person has or hasn't seen, or what a new clarity might be about. My biggest risk is writing as if a specific insight is already arriving, when the record only names the capacity. The ask survives being wrong because it points to the capacity in action, not to content; if the person is already clear, the ask is trivial rather than false. The sentence that serves me more than them is the sheet line that tries to name their condition instead of handing them the seeing.
